properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Wish 14 from the dev_storyflow agent, 2026-09-04. Nothing is intent.

WHAT HAPPENED TO THEM, in their words: "I recall writing 'nobody has ever watched two people play' THREE TIMES, once INTO AN ACCEPTED DECISION — WHILE A PASSING TWO-PERSON GROUP-PLAY VERIFICATION ALREADY EXISTED. I corrected it with a ChangeEvent."

⭐ THEIR DIAGNOSIS IS THE FINDING, AND IT NAMES TWO DIFFERENT SEARCHES. "The brainstorm and capture-intent skills both say SEARCH FOR DUPLICATES OF THE IDEA; neither says SEARCH FOR EVIDENCE AGAINST THE PREMISE. Those are different searches: THE DUPLICATE SEARCH LOOKS FOR NODES THAT SAY THE SAME THING, THE PREMISE SEARCH LOOKS FOR NODES THAT SAY THE OPPOSITE."

That distinction is exact, and everything reflow2 has built so far is on the first side of it. The duplicate guard, `search_first`, `distinct_from`, `refuse_unless_deliberate` — all of them ask "has somebody said this already?". Nothing asks "does the design already hold a measurement that makes this false?"

AND `detect_defects` DOES NOT COVER IT EITHER, for a reason they state precisely: "a Decision's premise is PROSE, NOT AN EDGE." `CONTRADICTS` exists and would model it, but only once somebody has already noticed — which is the thing that failed.

THEIR PROPOSAL: `add_decision` (or the brainstorm skill's step) runs the decision text against PASSING VERIFICATIONS and surfaces any whose findings contradict it — "a passing check exists whose name overlaps your premise; read it before accepting." They add, and it is the right caveat: "IT WOULD NOT BE EXACT, AND IT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT THIS ONE."

⭐ THE MACHINERY IS ALREADY THERE. The duplicate guard is BM25 over node text; pointing the same index at Verifications and their `findings`, scoped to `passing`, is the same query with a different filter. It would be a REPORT, not a refusal — consistent with `dec:report-dont-judge` and with how `search_first` already offers candidates rather than blocking.

⚠️ THE OBJECTION, recorded beside it: a keyword overlap between a decision's prose and a check's name is WEAK EVIDENCE, and this project has one measured instance of exactly that failure mode — dev_storyflow's own `planned`-capability sweep returned ten hits of which four were NEGATIONS, matched on the word "built". A premise check would inherit that: "nobody has watched two people play" and a check named "two people play" overlap strongly and mean opposite things, WHICH IS THE POINT — but so do a hundred honest pairs, and a guard that fires on those is the noise every other finding in this batch complains about.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the overlap would have been strong enough in their actual case. The claim is theirs, second-hand from a compaction summary by their own admission, and neither the decision text nor the verification name has been read here.
properties.name: OPEN — a decision was accepted on a premise the graph already held a passing check against. Should capture search for evidence AGAINST an idea, not only for duplicates of it?
properties.rationale: Captured under the brainstorm skill; recorded as an idea, nothing promoted. This is the only item in either 2026-09-04 feedback document that proposes a NEW KIND of check rather than a fix to an existing one, which is why it gets its own node rather than folding into the constructor-ergonomics idea.
